reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh responding favorably to Isaac's prayer (וַיֵּעָ֤תֶר לוֹ֙ יְהוָ֔ה - 'and the Lord answered his prayer') by enabling Rebekah to conceive. Additionally, Yahweh directly engages with Rebekah through prophecy, revealing the future of her children. The passage portrays Yahweh as responsive to the prayers of the Hebrew patriarchs and actively involved in fulfilling divine promises to them. Any conflicts present are interpersonal (between brothers Jacob and Esau), not antagonistic relationships between Yahweh and the Hebrew people.
